draft_revision: Initial review covered inherited v5 lifecycle_repair and comparability_rule_draft. Root owns subsequent protocol updates. No original draft hash is invented.

material_findings.finding: Current evaluator rejects v6 and all explicit-tier studies; it does not read captured service-tier evidence for wall comparability.
material_findings.change: Explicit v6-only admission, retain schema2 literal/compact/development cohort and freeze requested priority, high reasoning and the machine comparability rule.

material_findings.finding: Producer actual_served_status can be provider_reported_complete even when per-response tiers differ and actual_served is null.
material_findings.change: Recompute from all observations joined to exactly the unique assistant IDs in the hashed messages array; do not infer uniformity from producer summary fields.

material_findings.finding: Configured/requested priority does not prove provider-reported priority. Authored connectivity reports default.
material_findings.change: Uniform reported default across all36 is comparable under the declared rule, labeled default. Missing/mixed response tiers disable primary wall only; preserve quality, token counters and all paid costs.

material_findings.finding: Inherited lifecycle_repair describes first3v5 and idle-only repair with unchanged v4 code.
material_findings.change: Replace with current full non-assistant union correction and actual v6 rollout/freeze evidence. Extend pre_model_evidence with current correction, priority transport/connectivity, profiling and final verification artifacts.

admission_design: Keep unchanged exact shared success/cost/token/order projection; admit only exact named v6 ID plus required machine tier constants, descriptive extras allowed.

Require actual study.service_tier string priority and the existing exact development schema2/source_excerpt_equals/python.definition-prefix/1/compact cohort. Historical cohorts retain old semantics and reject explicit tiers.

Verify terminal artifact inventory first, then use the same session/evidence/messages.json used by the observer and session/evidence/service-tier.json; configuration and observed-model identity are independently bound to the frozen request.

Every unique assistant record must join exactly one response-tier observation; no duplicate, orphan, omitted, incomplete or unsupported scalar may be counted as covered. Match finite nonbool completion timestamps to the exported message.
Compute complete coverage for every trial, then one uniform global provider-reported value across all36; do not allow within-arm or per-trial averages to mask cross-arm variation.

Apply tier wall restriction before winning-metric determination; retain independent existing timing-caveat wall restriction, all raw wall values and token/quality evidence. No filtering/retries/pooling.
authored_tests_proposed: Exact v6 rule/cohort/priority admission and rejection of altered rules, unknown IDs, old manual-note/full cohorts, or missing tier policy.
All36 complete uniform default responses requested as priority admit wall; uniform priority does too.
Mixed tiers within one session or across arms/trials disable only wall and retain all token/cost/quality totals.
Producer complete/actual_served/id booleans cannot override inconsistent response rows.
Missing, duplicate, orphan observations; partial export; zero assistants; invalid tier scalar; absent/nonfinite/bool/mismatched completion time produce explicit noncomparability.
Hash-valid configuration/request/reasoning mismatch does not establish the tier cohort.
Actual reported fallback differs from requested priority without operational relabeling; no fast-service or billing inference.
Legacy reports stay byte/semantic compatible; explicit-tier studies cannot relabel old IDs; existing timing caveats and fixed all-six-pair rules still apply.
scope_limits: Response metadata is a pinned runtime projection taken before public native scrub, not independently verified wire scheduling, entitlement or billing.

Coverage is every exported assistant record; it is not an inventory of every provider request. Compaction/native metadata may represent other model work and must not be described as covered assistant responses.
No tracked edits, tests, model calls, Docker or heavy packaging in this design-review phase.
